text: A configuration rollback of rwb-access moves the four tables of this service that carry a version label of their own: permission by matrix_version, masking_rule by masking_version, role_conflict by conflict_version and delegation_limit by limit_version. It is a state and date change on the rows already stored and never a copy: the withdrawn rows go to ROLLED_BACK with valid_to yesterday (is_active false and state ROLLED_BACK for permission, which has no date column) and the restored rows go to IN_FORCE with valid_to null, so every row keeps its id. The version before the named one is the label that was in force immediately before it in the same table, read by valid_from for the three dated tables and by the label order fixed at the contract review for permission. The role list carries no version column in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and no role row is moved. Rule package versions (P7) and reference-data versions (P3), and the gate in front of them, are RWB-P4-AD013's and are not touched here.
why: The legacy story says any versioned table and the sources name no operation, no row model and no version-before rule for the tables rwb-access owns; a rollback written as a delete or a copy would break the queue, role and level a case already holds and would leave the audit with no evidence that the bad version was ever in force, while a rollback that also moved rule or reference versions would write another owner's tables.
read: RWB-E8-011 AC1; FSD P4 v3 A2.22 and A2.3 AC-ALT-P4-003-01; TSD P4 v3 T3.0, T3.1 (DF-REF-044, DF-REF-202, DF-REF-209, DF-REF-055) and T3.2; R-UNI-38; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01 and DP-13
applied_in: RWB-P4-E8011-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 7 (AC4), 8 (BR1 to BR3), 9, 11, 12.7; RWB-P4-E8011-CON sections 7 (AC2, AC3), 8, 11, 12.7
confirm: Security administrator and the tech leads of the four tables' stories at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8011-CON
impact: If a table needs a different model, only ConfigRollbackRepository and its updates change; a copy or delete model would instead break the record-ID rule the FSD states and would need a new column to keep the identity.

text: The effective moment of a rollback is now: the withdrawn rows close at yesterday and the restored rows are open-ended, and the request carries no date. A rollback cannot be back-dated and cannot be scheduled ahead.
why: The legacy criterion asks that a version be returned to its previous version and recorded, and the only worked rollback of the FSD is immediate; a submitted date would let a rollback re-decide work that has already been reported, and the request field set is not defined by any source.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.3 AC-ALT-P4-003-01 and AC-EXC-P4-003-02; A2.22; R-UNI-38; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-025, DF-REF-026, DF-REF-203, DF-REF-204, DF-REF-210, DF-REF-211
confirm: Security administrator and Internal audit at the contract review
impact: If a dated rollback is needed later, it is an additive field within major version 1 plus a rule on the earliest date; the row statements and the two record entries do not change.

text: A rollback needs the U letter in the capability area that owns the target kind: PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION for PERMISSION_MATRIX, MASKING_PROFILE and ROLE_CONFLICT, which TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives to RW-PLATADM as CRUD and to RW-SECADM as CRUDA, and RULES_AND_PARAMETERS for DELEGATION_LIMIT, where RW-COE holds CRUD and the T6.1 refinement gives it U and roll back while RW-RISK holds RA and no U. The legacy permission table's C for RW-COE and A for RW-RISK is read as the load and approval letters of those tables, which belong to RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD016-APP and RWB-P4-E1038-APP, not as the rollback letter. A caller without U in the area is refused 403 with MSG-P4-002.
why: Three sources disagree on who may undo a configuration version: the legacy story makes the platform administrator primary and gives the C letter to RW-COE and the A letter to RW-RISK, T6.1 gives RW-PLATADM R only in Rules and parameters, and the FSD names the platform administrator as the primary role of the feature; a story that silently granted the C or the A letter would contradict the matrix.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.22.3.3; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and its rule-package and workflow refinement; legacy RWB-E8-011 permission checks; Template and Rules v1 §R3 R-PREC and §R5.5 DP-08
confirm: Security administrator with the owner of the permission matrix and the CoE lead at the P4 design review
impact: If the matrix is corrected to give RW-PLATADM CRUD in Rules and parameters, only the area-to-letter row and the SIT users change; the two operations and their refusals do not.

text: A rollback appends exactly two entries to the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library, in the transaction that moves the rows: a withdrawal entry and a restoration entry, each carrying the target kind, the withdrawn and restored labels, the rowsWithdrawn and rowsRestored counts, the caller reference, the reason and the time, and each with its outbox row on rwb.decision-record.v1. The two record codes are not in any source, so they are the library's administrative-change codes fixed at the contract review; the answer carries the two entry ids as decisionRecordRefs, and the read of a rollback answers the stored answer and never recomputes it. MSG-P3-015 is carried as a message ID and its text is supplied by the message catalogue.
why: The legacy criterion requires the rollback to be recorded with the rule version and legacy AC2 requires nothing to change when the log cannot be written, but no source names the code of an administrative change or the fields of its entry, and the FSD names MSG-P3-015 without its wording; without fixed codes and fields neither criterion can be tested and the audit consumer cannot filter the entries.
read: RWB-E8-011 AC1 and AC2; FSD P4 v3 A2.3 AC-EXC-P4-003-02 and A2.22.4.1; TSD P4 v3 T6.3; LDM v8 DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-03 and DP-09; R-UNI-39
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-decision (P7) as the ledger owner, with Internal audit, at the contract review
impact: A different code changes the value written on every rollback entry and the filter the audit consumer uses; the two facts, their fields and the 503 of an unwritable record stay as specified.
